V has no prior trade — I'm free to initiate. With MA already at 12% and performing well (+7.40%), adding V creates diversification within the payments theme at a smaller weight (4%). The consumer spending resilience thesis supporting MA also supports V. At $365, V is near the middle of its 30-day range ($360.75-$367). Sizing modestly at 4% given we're near fully invested and just funded ORCL addition.

However, at 9.65% weight and +10% gain, it's prudent to trim partial profits and redeploy into a stronger near-term catalyst (ORCL). The position was last sold on 2026-07-27 (SELL), then re-bought. Reducing to 7% is a modest trim, not an exit — preserving the core aerospace exposure while generating cash for the ORCL opportunity.

recent_trades.summary: Re-entering ORCL on material new catalyst: Google Cloud AI partnership expansion announced today, driving 3.3% price jump.
recent_trades.reasoning: I sold ORCL on July 13 at ~$128. Today, ORCL popped 3.3% on news of a Google Cloud AI partnership expansion — this is a concrete, specific new fundamental catalyst that did not exist when I exited. The partnership signals cloud/AI revenue growth acceleration for Oracle, aligning with the broader AI infrastructure buildout theme. Sentiment is positive (+0.16). Current price ~$125 is actually below my prior sell price, offering a favorable re-entry. The AI CapEx/cloud tailwind is structural. I'll take a modest 5% position to capture this move without over-concentrating. The anti-reversal rule requires naming what changed: the Google Cloud AI partnership expansion announced today is the specific new information.

recent_trades.reasoning: The AI narrative is fracturing. Headlines indicating star AI investor Leopold Aschenbrenner is unwinding trades after steep losses suggests that the speculative excess in the sector is facing a wave of forced selling, making NVDA highly vulnerable as the sector bellwether.

The stock is only slightly lower on the day despite the headline, suggesting limited negative read-through and room for the catalyst to be digested further. I am increasing an existing winner but keeping size below 10% because the market backdrop is still mildly negative and I do not want to chase aggressively.

recent_trades.summary: Adding back to MA from 9.3% to ~12% on a concrete Q2 2026 earnings beat with strong consumer spending and cross-border payment growth — a new catalyst since yesterday's trim.
recent_trades.reasoning: I trimmed MA yesterday (2026-07-29) from 13.1% to ~9% primarily to fund energy adds and on negative MA sentiment. Today MA reported Q2 2026 earnings that beat estimates, with strong consumer spending and cross-border payments growth highlighted. This is a direct fundamental reversal of the negative sentiment that drove my trim. Payment network volume growth and cross-border recovery are the core MA thesis drivers and they are now confirmed for Q2. Current price $570.64 vs my avg cost $526.94 means I'm adding into a +8.3% unrealized gain position, which is acceptable given the earnings confirmation. The target weight of 12% stays within the 20% limit.

recent_trades.summary: Trimming HON from ~4.9% to ~2% as the industrial automation thesis has weakened with Carrier falling despite an earnings beat, and freeing capital for higher-conviction MA add.
recent_trades.reasoning: HON is down 4.20% from entry. Today's Carrier news (beat estimates, raised outlook, fell anyway) signals the market is not rewarding industrial names even on good fundamentals. My original thesis was industrial/AI automation beneficiary but the conviction has dropped. Trimming to a small residual frees ~$3,200 for the MA re-add. I keep a small position in case industrial sentiment reverses.

Proceeds help fund higher-conviction additions while respecting single-name limits.
